traceability.evidence:
Rule implementation: - src/rules/require-branch-annotation.ts defines the ESLint rule: - Meta: - type: "problem" - docs.description: "Require @story and @req annotations on code branches" - messages.missingAnnotation: "Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}." - schema with configurable `branchTypes` array - create(context): - Calls validateBranchTypes(context) - If validateBranchTypes returns a listener (invalid config), returns it directly - Otherwise iterates over branchTypes (e.g. IfStatement, SwitchCase, TryStatement, loops) and for each type registers a handler that calls reportMissingAnnotations(context, node, storyFixCountRef) - Special-cases SwitchCase with null test (default) to skip it as insignificant - File annotated with story and requirements: - @story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md - @req REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE
- src/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.ts provides the branch-specific logic: - DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES constant: - ["IfStatement", "SwitchCase", "TryStatement", "CatchClause", "ForStatement", "ForOfStatement", "ForInStatement", "WhileStatement", "DoWhileStatement"] - Annotated with @story 004.0 and @req REQ-SIGNIFICANCE-CRITERIA - validateBranchTypes(context): - Reads context.options[0].branchTypes - If branchTypes is an array: - Filters out invalid values by checking inclusion in DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES - If any invalid types exist, returns a RuleListener { Program: ProgramHandler } - ProgramHandler reports for each invalid type: - message: `Value "${t}" should be equal to one of the allowed values: ${DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES.join(', ')}` - If no invalid, returns the configured branchTypes - If branchTypes is not provided, returns a copy of DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES - Implements REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE and configuration error handling - gatherBranchCommentText(sourceCode, node): - For SwitchCase: - Looks up to PRE_COMMENT_OFFSET (2) lines above the case, collecting line comments or block comments matching /^\s*(\/\/|\/\*)/ - Returns joined comment text - For other nodes: - Uses sourceCode.getCommentsBefore(node) - Maps each comment node to its `value` and joins into a single string - Annotated with REQ-COMMENT-ASSOCIATION and specific traceability requirements - getBranchAnnotationInfo(sourceCode, node) (internal): - Uses gatherBranchCommentText to obtain comment text - missingStory = !/@story\b/.test(text) - missingReq = !/@req\b/.test(text) - Computes indent and insertPos for auto-fix insertion - reportMissingStory(context, node, { indent, insertPos, storyFixCountRef }): - If storyFixCountRef.count === 0: offers fixer inserting - `${indent}// @story .story.md\n` at insertPos - Reports messageId "missingAnnotation" with data { missing: "@story" } - Increments storyFixCountRef - Else: reports missingAnnotation without fixer - reportMissingReq(context, node, { indent, insertPos, missingStory }): - If !missingStory: offers fixer inserting `${indent}// @req \n` - Otherwise: reports missingAnnotation without fixer - reportMissingAnnotations(context, node, storyFixCountRef): - Gets { missingStory, missingReq, indent, insertPos } - Builds actions array for story and req - For each action with missing = true, calls the corresponding report function - These implement REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION, REQ-COMMENT-ASSOCIATION, REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, and performance-conscious behavior (limited scanning of lines, simple regex checks)
Integration into plugin configs: - src/index.ts: - RULE_NAMES includes "require-branch-annotation" ensuring the rule module is dynamically loaded: - const RULE_NAMES = ["require-story-annotation", "require-req-annotation", "require-branch-annotation", ...] as const; - Dynamic loader requires ./rules/${name} and assigns rules[name] = mod.default ?? mod - TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES maps: - "traceability/require-branch-annotation": "error" - createTraceabilityFlatConfig() returns configs that include this rule severity - configs.recommended and configs.strict are arrays of this flat config, so the rule is part of preset configurations, satisfying integration-related DoD item
Tests (behavior verification and coverage of requirements): - tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts: - File-level annotations explicitly reference the story and requirements: - @story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md - @req REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION (rule enforces branch annotations) - Sets up RuleTester with ecmaVersion 2020 - runRule helper wraps ruleTester.run("require-branch-annotation", rule, tests) - describe block: "Require Branch Annotation Rule (Story 004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS)" - First runRule invocation validates main behavior: - VALID cases include: - Switch with fallback scanning comment detection for SwitchCase; ensures gatherBranchCommentText’s custom logic is exercised - IfStatement with inline // @story and // @req - ForStatement with block comments /* @story ... */ and /* @req ... */ - Switch with annotated case and unannotated default (valid default case without annotations), aligning with significance criteria (default considered trivial) - Try-finally and catch blocks with annotations on TryStatement and CatchClause - Do-while, for-of, for-in, and while loops with annotations - Configurable-scope behavior: - With options [{ branchTypes: ["IfStatement"] }], an unannotated switch is valid (unlisted branch type is ignored) - With options [{ branchTypes: ["IfStatement", "SwitchCase"] }], annotated if with story/req is valid - INVALID cases cover missing annotations and auto-fix behavior across all branch types: - IfStatement without any annotations: - Expected output inserts `// @story .story.md` above the if - Errors: missingAnnotation with { missing: "@story" } and { missing: "@req" } - For loop with only @story: - Expected output inserts `// @req ` below story - Error only for missing "@req" - While loop with only @req: - Expected output inserts `// @story .story.md` below existing req - Error only for missing "@story" - Switch case without annotations (including variant with a blank line before case): - Expected output adds story comment before case - Errors for both missing "@story" and "@req" - Do-while, for-of, for-in loops without annotations, with expected auto-fix and both missing annotations - Try-catch without annotations: - Expected output inserts a single story before try - Errors for both missing annotations on try and both on catch - Configurable-scope invalid case for ForStatement only, enforcing detection and auto-fix on configured branch type - Second runRule invocation tests configuration error behavior (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE and REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION edge handling): - invalid case: options [{ branchTypes: ["UnknownType"] }] - Expects an error whose message matches /should be equal to one of the allowed values/ - Confirms that invalid branchTypes are reported during linting, aligning with the story’s "Invalid Configuration Behavior" example
- tests/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.test.ts: - Header references story 004.0 and REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE - Tests validateBranchTypes: - Returns DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES when no options provided - Returns provided valid branchTypes array when types are valid - When invalid types are provided: - Returns a listener object with Program handler - Calling Program(fakeNode) triggers context.report once per invalid type - Confirms message contains `Value "${t}" should be equal to one of the allowed values:` - This directly validates configuration handling and error reporting behavior described in the story and docs
Test execution evidence: - Ran targeted tests for this rule: - Command executed via tooling: - npm test -- --runTestsByPath tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts --verbose - Under the hood, this runs: - jest --ci --bail --runTestsByPath tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts --verbose - The tool did not report any failures or non-zero exit code, indicating the tests for this story pass successfully. - Earlier, the full test suite command was also run without failure: - npm test -- --ci --no-watchAll --verbose - Which runs: jest --ci --bail --ci --no-watchAll --verbose
Documentation (REQ-DOCUMENTATION and Configuration details): - docs/rules/require-branch-annotation.md: - Describes the rule purpose: - "Ensures that significant code branches (if/else, switch cases, loops, try/catch) have `@story` and `@req` annotations for traceability." - Explicit story and requirements linkage: - @story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md - @req REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION, @req REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE - Rule details: - Explains that it checks comments immediately preceding significant branches and ensures both @story and @req are present - Options: - Documents `branchTypes` option, default values (matching DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES) and allowed values - Describes invalid configuration behavior: error message when an invalid type is provided - Examples: - Correct example: if with @story and @req above it - Incorrect example: unannotated if - Invalid configuration example: branchTypes: ["IfStatement", "InvalidType"] with documented error message pattern - This satisfies the story’s documentation acceptance criterion, including configuration and practical examples
Story traceability and requirement mapping: - Implementation files (src/rules/require-branch-annotation.ts and src/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.ts) are richly annotated with: - @story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md - @req tags for: REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-SIGNIFICANCE-CRITERIA, REQ-COMMENT-ASSOCIATION, REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING, and additional traceability-focused helper requirements - Test files for this rule and its helpers explicitly reference the story and key requirements, ensuring bidirectional traceability between spec and implementation/tests.
traceability.notes:
All key aspects of story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md are implemented and verified:
- Core Functionality (branch detection and annotation enforcement): - The require-branch-annotation rule targets all significant branch node types (if, switch cases, try/catch, loops) via DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES and per-type handlers. - Helper functions gatherBranchCommentText and getBranchAnnotationInfo correctly associate preceding comments with branches and determine whether @story and @req are present using regex checks. - Tests cover missing annotations and auto-fix behavior across every relevant branch type, validating both detection and error/fix behavior.
- Quality Standards and Integration: - The rule uses a clear meta schema, separates concerns into helper utilities, and respects ESLint best practices (RuleTester-based tests, clean RuleModule definition, configurable options). - It is integrated into the plugin export and included in both recommended and strict configs through TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES and createTraceabilityFlatConfig, ensuring real-world usability.
- User Experience and Error Handling: - Error messages are specific: `Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}.` with data distinguishing `@story` vs `@req`. - Invalid configuration for branchTypes yields a clear configuration error indicating allowed values, as demonstrated by tests and the helper’s implementation. - Edge cases, such as SwitchCase default branches and SwitchCase comments separated by blank lines, are handled explicitly and covered in tests.
- Configuration and Documentation: - The branchTypes option is implemented as described, with defaults, allowed values, and runtime validation. - Documentation in docs/rules/require-branch-annotation.md matches the implemented behavior and provides usage and configuration examples, along with invalid configuration behavior.
Given the concrete implementation, thorough unit tests specifically tied to this story, successful test execution, and dedicated documentation, this story’s acceptance criteria and technical requirements are fully satisfied.
